attributes.function: trains, certifies and holds the seals of surveyors; keeps the master level and the reference brines
attributes.grievance: when it learns of it, the charge will not be that he found water. It will be that he carried the College seal to the centre of the plain and brought back a number it cannot vouch for: a sealed surveyor who files nothing is indistinguishable from a Warden with a lead stamp, and the seal is the only thing the College owns. The remedy in its own statutes is to lift it — which ends his surveying and puts a question mark against every level he ever certified.
attributes.house_rule: a level is a level and the ground does not care who owns it; a finding is entered on the College roll before it is shown to the body that commissioned it. The entry is short — surveyor, ground, date, one line of result — and it is made before the packet is stitched. It is the College's whole defence against a commissioner who does not care for the number he paid for.
attributes.instruments: the water-glass, the chain, the master level at the far rim
attributes.relationship_to_wardens: the Wardenry cannot lawfully survey without College-sealed surveyors, and the College cannot reach the plain without the Wardenry's licences. Neither can do without the other and neither likes it.
attributes.seat: the far rim, opposite Bell Harrow
attributes.the_rule_broken: Denet Rasca sealed the centre survey in the spring of RR 203 and entered nothing. There is no line against his name on the RR 203 roll and no clerk at the far rim who can swear to what he found. The College's lead sits on a packet holding a finding the College has never seen.
attributes.weakness: no money, no wagons, no enforcement — it can prove a thing to the last decimal and do absolutely nothing about it

name: The College of Levels
summary: The chartered surveyors' college on the far rim, which trains and seals every person permitted to set an instrument on the Meniscus and put a number to what they see. It certifies the Wardenry's surveyors but does not employ them, so a Warden-surveyor carries two loyalties and one seal. Its house rule — that a finding is entered on the roll before it is shown to anyone — is the only hold it has on the numbers that go out under its lead. Denet Rasca sealed the water survey without entering it, and the College does not yet know.
